sections.html:
Greenwich is the southwesternmost town in both Connecticut and New England, home to 63,518 people in 2020. Port Chester, Rye Brook and North Castle in New York lie to the west, Stamford to the east and the Sound to the south. ZIP codes are 06830, 06831, 06870 and 06878.

The town is a single taxing body, yet buyers think in sections. Cos Cob, Old Greenwich and Riverside have their own postal names, Byram, Glenville, Pemberwick and Rock Ridge are separate villages, and the Back Country, Mid-Country, Belle Haven and Mianus are informal labels that agents use all the time. Two things shape value more than most: the commute (four Metro-North stations, with express trains to Grand Central in about 50 minutes and locals in about 60) and water. Old Greenwich, Riverside and Byram sit near the shore, so flood zone status is a routine question, while the Back Country north of the Merritt Parkway gets more snow than the coast.

The Planning and Zoning and Wetlands offices can speak to a particular address.

One combined bill covers real estate, personal property and motor vehicles. Bills are mailed in June, payment is due July 1, and the latest cycle on the Tax Collector's page made the bill delinquent after August 3. Dates can move from year to year, so read the current bill.

The office is in Town Hall at 101 Field Point Road, Room 145, open Monday to Friday from 8:30 am to 3:30 pm. The phone is 203-622-7891.

Way to payFee
In person or by mail (check, money order, cash in person)No fee
Online, electronic funds transfer$2.00 per transaction, paid to the vendor
Online, card, Apple Pay or Google Pay2.50 percent of the payment, paid to the vendor
Returned payment$20.00 plus possible interest

Late real estate bills accrue interest up to a stated date, and any property still carrying a balance is liened in May. If you are behind, ask the office for a payoff figure before you choose a closing date.

sections.h2: Where to file a Greenwich assessment appeal
sections.html:
The elected Board of Assessment Appeals takes these filings. The Assessor's Office will not accept appeal forms, which surprises people who assume the assessor is the right door. The Board's page has the form and the email address, boardofassessmentappeals@greenwichct.org.

Real estate and personal property filings are due in February at 5:00 pm under Connecticut General Statutes section 12-111; for the 2025 Grand List the date was February 20. Hearings are held in person at Town Hall in March. Ask the Board for the date that applies to the 2026 Grand List before you count on any day.

  • An appeal challenges the assessment only. The mill rate is set separately by the Board of Estimate and Taxation in May.
  • The Board can raise, lower or leave a value alone, and decisions are mailed roughly two weeks after the last hearing.
  • Owners who still disagree have 60 days from the notice to go to Connecticut Superior Court.
  • Commercial, industrial, utility and apartment property assessed above $1,000,000 may be skipped for hearings.

The Board has five members, elected every two years in odd years.

When the deed is recorded, the seller or the seller's attorney files Form OP-236 with the state. Greenwich's town code on that form is 057. Tax is due once consideration reaches $2,000, unless the transfer is exempt.

The exempt list on the Department of Revenue Services tax information page takes in transfers between spouses, a deed in lieu of foreclosure on a principal residence, and a principal residence sold for less than its mortgages and tax liens add up to. Your closing agent or the Town Clerk's office can tell you which line fits.

sections.h2: Selling a Greenwich house with taxes owed
sections.html:
Back tax does not close the door on a sale. The balance is paid from what you receive at closing, so the main job is knowing the number early. The usual sequence looks like this.

  1. Ask the Tax Collector for a payoff on the real estate account, including interest.
  2. Find out whether a lien was recorded. Properties with a balance are liened in May, and a release has to be part of the closing.
  3. Hand the payoff to your closing attorney, who builds it into the settlement statement.
  4. Set the closing date after the lien question is answered, not before.

Bring the bill, a photo ID and, for an estate, the papers that show who can sign. Greenwich is a place where one missed May date can turn a small balance into a lien, so owners who are even a little behind should call sooner rather than later.

Because Greenwich mixes shoreline neighborhoods, village centers and the Back Country, a seller's situation depends heavily on the street. Houses with deferred repairs are slow on the open market. Estates often need time to settle who owns the property before anyone can list. Owners behind on tax may be facing a May lien and need a closing date that clears it.

A cash sale is one path for people who want a fixed closing date. The buyer takes the house as-is, repairs are off your list, and open tax comes out of the proceeds. It is worth comparing with the cost of fixing the house and carrying it through another bill.

sections.h2: Beaches, water and what buyers ask
sections.html: Greenwich has four beaches on the Sound: Greenwich Point, Byram Beach, Island Beach and Great Captain Island. After a 2001 court ruling in Leydon v. Greenwich, all four are open to non-residents too. For a seller, the practical side of the shoreline is flood zone mapping, drainage and the age of docks or seawalls. Buyers on the water often want insurance history before they make an offer, so gather it early.

faqs.q: When are Greenwich property taxes due?
faqs.a: Payment is due July 1, and the bill turns delinquent a few weeks later. Check the Tax Collector's page each year, since mailing and delinquency dates can change.

faqs.q: Where do I file a Greenwich assessment appeal?
faqs.a: With the Board of Assessment Appeals, not the Assessor. The Board's email is boardofassessmentappeals@greenwichct.org.

faqs.q: Who sets the Greenwich mill rate?
faqs.a: The Board of Estimate and Taxation sets it in May. An assessment appeal does not change the rate.

faqs.q: What happens to Greenwich real estate that stays delinquent?
faqs.a: Interest builds up to a set date, and any property with a balance is liened in May. Call the Tax Collector for a payoff before you set a closing date.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Greenwich house if I owe back taxes?
faqs.a: Yes. Unpaid tax comes out of the proceeds at closing, and a cash sale can close on a date you choose.
